reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure. Let J be a natural number with J>=2. Let V:E->R be genuinely twice continuously Frechet differentiable, and let kappa be a nonnegative real with kappa>=1. Assume, for all x,v in E,
  kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Fix real eta,c,epsilon with 0<eta<=c<1 and epsilon>0. Let nu be a probability measure on E x E and fix xstar in E with grad V(xstar)=0. Fix h,M in R with h>0 and M>=0. Assume that s=(X,P) -> ||X-xstar||^2+||P||^2 is Bochner integrable with respect to nu, with its integral <=M.
For the J actual indices i,j in Fin(J)={0,...,J-1}, define precisely
  t_i=(h/2)(1-cos((i/(J-1))pi)),
  ell_j(X)=product_{k in Fin(J),k!=j} (t_j-t_k)^(-1)(X-t_k),
  Lambda=sup{sum_j |ell_j(s)| : s in [0,h]},
  omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i} (t_i-s)ell_j(s) ds,
  pw_j=omega_{J-1,j},
  bw_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s) ds,
  S=(h^2/2)Lambda.
Here the quotient in the node formula is real; the ell_j are real Lagrange polynomials evaluated at real s; Lambda is the real supremum of the displayed interval image; all interval integrals use real Lebesgue measure with orientation. pw,bw denote positionWeight,momentumWeight.
Write D=dim_R E, a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)). Let G be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability measure on E. Set gi=product_{Fin(J)} G, gamma=(G x G) x (gi x gi), and mu=nu x gamma. All noise factors are independent: two E-valued Gaussian vectors and two independent J-coordinate Gaussian arrays whose own coordinates are independent. Under mu the incoming state of law nu is independent of this noise. Define exactly
  MR=M+(1-exp(-h))D,
  B=6 MR+3 epsilon^2+3 eta D,
  C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c),
  L0=C[1+log(1+sqrt(2 MR)/epsilon)],
  L1=C[1+log(1+sqrt(4 MR+2 S^2 B)/epsilon)].
If h^2 Lambda<=1, there exist single global measurable maps p,q:E->E and N:E->N such that, for every y in E,
  p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y,
  ||q(y)-p(y)||<=epsilon,
  proximalQuery(grad V,eta,epsilon,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1),
and p is nonexpansive: ||p(u)-p(v)||<=||u-v|| for all u,v in E.
The interpreter proximalQuery(g,eta,epsilon,y,fuel,x) returns none at zero fuel. With fuel n+1 it evaluates g(x), sets z=y-eta g(x), and tests ||z-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon. On success it returns some(x,1); otherwise it recurses at z with fuel n, propagates failure and increments a successful count by one. The equivalent residual threshold is ||x+eta g(x)-y||<=(1-eta)epsilon. The terminal successful gradient/residual test is counted. N(y)+1 is a finite successful execution certificate with no claim of free precomputation of the fuel/count.
For those same p,q,N and full input w=((X,P),((zeta0,zeta1),(G0,G1))), define the approximate phase by
  P0(w)=a P+sigma zeta0,
  Y0_i(w)=X+t_i P0(w),
  Z0_j(w)=grad V(q(Y0_j(w))+sqrt(eta)G0_j),
  Y1_i(w)=Y0_i(w)-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j(w),
  Z1_j(w)=grad V(q(Y1_j(w))+sqrt(eta)G1_j),
  Phi(w)=(X+h P0(w)-sum_j pw_j Z1_j(w),
          a(P0(w)-sum_j bw_j Z1_j(w))+sigma zeta1),
  T(w)=2J+sum_i[(N(Y0_i(w))+1)+(N(Y1_i(w))+1)] in N.
Define the exact implicit-map phase, using the same P0,Y0 and supplied noise coordinates, by
  Z0p_j(w)=grad V(p(Y0_j(w))+sqrt(eta)G0_j),
  Y1p_i(w)=Y0_i(w)-sum_j omega_ij Z0p_j(w),
  Z1p_j(w)=grad V(p(Y1p_j(w))+sqrt(eta)G1_j),
  Phip(w)=(X+h P0(w)-sum_j pw_j Z1p_j(w),
           a(P0(w)-sum_j bw_j Z1p_j(w))+sigma zeta1).
In particular the exact second stage uses Y1p, not the approximate Y1.
On the state space Q=E x E use the explicit distance
  d2((X,P),(Xprime,Pprime))=sqrt(||X-Xprime||^2+||P-Pprime||^2).
For real rho and measures alpha,beta on Q define the extended-nonnegative quantity
  W_rho(alpha,beta)=[inf_{tau measure on Q x Q: tau.fst=alpha,tau.snd=beta}
                       integral^- (ENNReal.ofReal(d2(s,sprime)))^rho dtau(s,sprime)]^(rho^(-1)).
This is the infimum over all coupling measures with the two specified marginals of the lower integral of the powered cost, followed by the inverse-rho real power. ENNReal.ofReal embeds max(real value,0); powers are real powers in extended nonnegative reals. The metric is the displayed square-root sum of squared position and momentum norms, not an unspecified default product norm.
Then Phi and T are measurable, and there exist Markov kernels Kp,Kq:Q->Q with probability outputs satisfying, simultaneously,
  Kp(s)=(z -> Phip(s,z))_* gamma for every incoming s,
  Kq(s)=(z -> Phi(s,z))_* gamma for every incoming s,
  phaseQuery(grad V,eta,epsilon,h,t,omega,pw,bw,(y -> N(y)+1),w)
    =some(Phi(w),T(w)) for every full input w,
  w -> (T(w):R) is Bochner integrable under mu,
  integral (T(w):R) dmu(w) <= (J:R)(2+L0+L1),
  W_rho(Kq(s),Kp(s)) <= ENNReal.ofReal(3 h Lambda epsilon)
    for every incoming state s and every real rho>=1.
phaseQuery is the supplied Option-valued finite program. In increasing Fin(J) order it executes the same proximalQuery at each first-stage Y0_i with fuel(Y0_i), anchor and initial iterate Y0_i. It maps a successful point/count (x,n) to (grad V(x+sqrt(eta)G0_i),n+1), collecting these actual gradient values and adding counts. Any failure returns none. It constructs second-stage inputs using the actually returned first gradients, then repeats the corresponding second array with G1, charging one shifted-gradient evaluation in addition to each actual proximal count. It returns the resulting full position/momentum state and the sum of both array counts. Thus T counts every actual interpreter evaluation, including each terminal successful test, plus one additional shifted-gradient query per node per stage, totaling an overhead of exactly 2J. No desired output or count is given as input to phaseQuery.
All sums range over the J actual nodes. The integral count bound uses precisely mu=nu x gamma, whereas the transport bound compares both one-step output laws at the same arbitrary incoming state and holds for every real rho>=1, including noninteger exponents with no upper restriction. These conclusions share the same witnesses p,q,N and kernels Kp,Kq. No assertion is made about an optimal coupling being attained, a free fuel-selection algorithm, elapsed time, sampler invariance or long-run convergence, comparison with a continuous-time dynamics, or the growth of Lambda.
